title: CDC PLACES county vintages move across distinct health and social-need surfaces
source_unit: Same county FIPS in selected CDC PLACES 2024 and 2025 releases, with 2023 CBP health-establishment capacity quartiles
geography: United States; 2,885 common county FIPS with capacity context

observations.period: PLACES 2024 release -> PLACES 2025 release; all common counties

denominator.unit: common county FIPS; social-needs measures available for 2,239 in 2024 and 2,255 in 2025

observations.method: FIPS intersection and unweighted county medians; PLACES 2024 uses primarily 2022 BRFSS inputs and PLACES 2025 uses primarily 2023 BRFSS inputs.
observations.uncertainty: Releases differ in BRFSS, Census population, ACS inputs, geography, measure definitions, and available county universes. This is not a same-resident panel or causal change estimate.
observations.subgroup: All common counties; no individual respondent or household linkage.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different measures move in different directions; a median change may reflect model/input/vintage differences rather than underlying local change.

observations.period: PLACES 2024 release -> PLACES 2025 release; low health-establishment-capacity quartile

denominator.unit: common county FIPS in the lowest quartile of 2023 CBP health establishments per 10,000

observations.method: Capacity quartile defined on common counties; unweighted county medians compared across PLACES vintages.
observations.uncertainty: Capacity is employer stock, not usable care; social-needs availability differs between vintages and values are modeled small-area estimates.
observations.subgroup: Lower visible health-establishment-capacity counties; no resident linkage.
observations.counterinterpretation: The apparent improvement in several social-need medians does not establish recovery or a capacity effect; model/input changes and neighboring access remain possible.

observations.period: PLACES 2024 release -> PLACES 2025 release; high health-establishment-capacity quartile

denominator.unit: common county FIPS in the highest quartile of 2023 CBP health establishments per 10,000

observations.method: Capacity quartile defined on common counties; unweighted county medians compared across PLACES vintages.
observations.uncertainty: The high-capacity group is not a treatment group; observed movement can reflect population, insurance, survey, model, geography, or measure changes.
observations.subgroup: Higher visible health-establishment-capacity counties; no resident linkage.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher food insecurity and insurance-loss medians despite greater establishment stock weaken a mechanical capacity-to-wellbeing interpretation.

related_sources.claim: CDC describes the 2024/2025 BRFSS, population, geography, and measure-vintage changes.
CDC documents the PLACES small-area estimation method and limitations.
Reproduction output for the same-county vintage comparison.

boundary: This is a descriptive vintage comparison of modeled county estimates. It does not estimate change for the same residents, local intervention effects, provider adequacy, patient access, household outcomes, trust, or political action.
